meta.description: OpsAPI is a self-hosted, multi-tenant API platform: one sign-in for every app, a workspace per customer, and 20 business modules from CRM and invoicing to CMS and UK tax filing. OpenResty, Lua and PostgreSQL, run on your own infrastructure under a licence.

header.title: OpsAPI
header.subtitle: One self-hosted API for sign-in, workspaces and business modules.
header.description: OpsAPI signs your users in once for every app, keeps each customer's data in its own workspace, and switches on the business modules a product needs, from CRM to UK tax filing. It is licensed software that runs on your own infrastructure.

intro.title: Stop building a backend per product
intro.body: Most teams that run several products end up with several backends, each with its own login, user table, roles and admin screens. OpsAPI replaces them with one. Sign-in, two-factor codes, Google, Apple and SAML single sign-on, workspaces, roles and API keys are always on. On top sit 20 business modules: CRM, invoicing, accounting, UK tax filing, kanban, chat, e-commerce, CMS, forms, hiring and more. One setting, PROJECT_CODE, chooses which modules a deployment loads; the rest have no routes and no tables. OpsAPI is built and run by Workstation, the company behind TenthMatrix, and it is the API this website's blog and contact form use.

screenshot.title: How OpsAPI fits together
screenshot.caption: Clients reach one OpenResty container through the edge. Lua runs inside the Nginx workers, so a request never hops to a separate app server. Dashed lines are connections made as needed: Redis, MinIO, Kafka and the model provider are optional, and a minimal deployment needs only PostgreSQL.
screenshot.alt: OpsAPI system overview: admin dashboard, web apps, mobile apps and scripts call an edge proxy, which forwards to the OpsAPI container (Nginx workers, before_filter, middleware, routes, queries, models) backed by PostgreSQL, Redis, MinIO or S3, Kafka, an LLM provider, Prometheus and external APIs

pillars.title: Four things it does for every product

items.title: One sign-in for every app
items.text: Email and password with lockout and rate limits, emailed two-factor codes, Google, Apple, SAML 2.0 and a hosted sign-in page. Any app checks a token with one call: /auth/me.

items.title: Workspaces from the first table
items.text: Each customer is a workspace with its own members, roles, invitations, mail settings and AI provider. Every query is scoped to the workspace.

items.title: 20 business modules
items.text: Switch on CRM, invoicing, accounting, tax filing, kanban, chat, e-commerce, CMS, forms, hiring and more, per deployment, with 16 ready-made presets.

items.title: Built to be run
items.text: One Docker image, a Helm chart with a migration job, health probes, Prometheus metrics, Grafana dashboards, an audit trail and a catalogue of error codes.

steps.title: One request, from client to database

items.title: Edge
items.text: TLS ends at the edge proxy, which routes by host name to the OpsAPI container.

items.title: Authenticate
items.text: Public paths skip sign-in; every other request needs a JWT or an opsk_ API key.

items.title: Pick the workspace
items.text: From a header, the token or the subdomain. Unknown, suspended or non-member: the request stops.

items.title: Check the permission
items.text: module.action permissions per role. Missing permission: 403.

items.title: Run the module
items.text: Only modules switched on by PROJECT_CODE have routes. Others answer 404 for everyone.

items.title: Resposta
items.text: Queries scoped to the workspace, a JSON reply, and any error returned with a code and a correlation id.

features.title: What is in the box
features.intro: 48 capabilities in five groups. Sign-in, workspaces and the platform layer are always on; business modules are switched per deployment.

items.title: SAML single sign-on per workspace
items.text: Each workspace connects its own identity provider, such as Okta, Entra ID, Google Workspace, OneLogin or Keycloak. Accounts are created on first sign-in and matched by email domain.

items.title: Roles and permissions
items.text: Owner, admin and member roles are seeded in every workspace. Permissions are module.action pairs, and the dashboard menu follows them.

items.title: API keys and audit
items.text: Long-lived keys for servers and scripts, scoped to a workspace. Sign-in events, user activity and an audit trail of changes per workspace.

items.title: Signed webhooks
items.text: Workspaces send their events to their own URLs, signed with HMAC-SHA256 and a timestamp, and retried for up to eight attempts.

items.title: Headless CMS
items.text: Pages and blog posts with media and categories. Publishing calls a signed webhook, so a static website rebuilds itself.

items.title: UK tax filing (HMRC MTD)
items.text: Bank statement extraction, AI classification and Making Tax Digital submission with the anti-fraud headers HMRC requires.

items.title: Plugins
items.text: Drop a folder of Lua in and it gets sign-in, workspaces, roles, migrations, dashboard pages, event listeners and scheduled jobs.

items.title: TypeScript SDK and OpenAPI
items.text: @opsapi/client gives typed calls for every endpoint, sign-in with two-factor, pagination, retries and webhook checks. The spec is at /openapi.json.

items.title: Secret vault
items.text: Encrypted secrets per workspace with pluggable vault providers.

agents.title: The business modules
agents.intro: Each module is a feature flag. A switched-off module is absent, not hidden: its addresses answer 'not found' and its tables are never created.

architecture.title: Lua inside Nginx, PostgreSQL underneath
architecture.intro: OpsAPI is a Lapis application that runs inside OpenResty's Nginx workers. A minimal deployment needs only PostgreSQL; Redis, MinIO, Kafka and an AI model are optional.

steps.title: Clients
steps.text: The admin dashboard, your web and mobile apps, servers and scripts, all on the same API and the same sign-in.

steps.title: OpenResty workers
steps.text: Lua runs in the Nginx worker processes: no proxy hop and no separate app server.

steps.title: Modules per deployment
steps.text: The PROJECT_CODE preset decides which modules load. A module that is not loaded has no routes and no tables.

steps.title: Serviços
steps.text: PostgreSQL with pgvector for every table, plus optional Redis, MinIO or S3, Kafka, Ollama or a hosted model, and Prometheus.

roadmap.title: Pick the modules per deployment
roadmap.intro: Choose one preset with PROJECT_CODE, or combine them, for example ecommerce,collaboration. Sign-in, workspaces and roles are always included. There are 16 presets in all.

aiAngle.title: Safe by default
aiAngle.intro: OpsAPI holds the logins and the data of every product that uses it, so the defaults are strict.
points: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt, with lockout after failed attempts and per-IP rate limits.
Short-lived JWTs, rotating refresh tokens in an HttpOnly cookie, and tokens issued only to allowed origins.
SAML responses that are tampered, wrapped, unsigned, replayed, expired or signed with SHA-1 are refused.
Every query is scoped to the workspace; platform admins are still scoped to the workspace they name.
Workspace owners decide whether members need two-factor codes. Platform admins always do.
The admin dashboard is designed to sit behind a VPN or zero-trust broker, not on the open internet.

deploy.title: Running in minutes
deploy.body: Run the bwalia/opsapi image from Docker Hub with PostgreSQL, or clone the repository and bring up the API, dashboard, PostgreSQL, Redis, MinIO, Kafka, Grafana and Prometheus with one script. For production, the Helm chart runs migrations before each upgrade and drains pods gracefully.

items.title: Blog: one API for every product

items.question: Is OpsAPI free?
items.answer: No. The source is on GitHub to read; running OpsAPI needs a licence. It is self-hosted, so there is no per-user fee. You run the PostgreSQL database, take its backups, upgrade OpsAPI and monitor it yourself, or ask TenthMatrix to do it for you.

items.question: What does it run on?
items.answer: OpenResty (Nginx with LuaJIT), the Lapis framework and PostgreSQL. Redis, MinIO or S3, Kafka and a model provider are optional; a minimal deployment needs only PostgreSQL. It ships as one Docker image and a Helm chart.

items.question: Can different customers see each other's data?
items.answer: Each customer is a workspace, and every query is scoped to it. A request with no workspace, an unknown or suspended workspace, or a user who is not a member is refused before any module code runs.

items.question: Can one deployment run only some modules?
items.answer: Yes. PROJECT_CODE picks the modules, using presets such as business, ecommerce, cms or tax_copilot, or core_only for sign-in and workspaces alone. Module sets are per deployment, not per workspace.

items.question: Which languages can call it?
items.answer: Any language that speaks HTTP. There is a TypeScript SDK, an OpenAPI spec and Swagger explorer, and sample apps in Java, PHP, Python, Rust and Go that share one sign-in.

items.question: Does it work with AI agents?
items.answer: The repository includes an MCP server, so Claude Code, Cursor or another MCP-capable agent can work with kanban tasks and website content using a personal API key, with every change logged as that user. Several modules also use AI: chat, accounting, tax filing, hiring and the shop, with Ollama or a hosted model.

items.question: Can I try it?
items.answer: Yes. opsapi.org/demo has a read-only dashboard that resets every 30 minutes, a SAML test identity provider and five sample apps signing in through one OpsAPI.
